sentences.text: Brontosaurus was a large, long-necked, quadrupedal herbivorous sauropod dinosaur with a long tail ending in a whip-like structure.

Its neck bones were extremely robust and heavily built compared to relatives like Diplodocus, while its short, stout forelimbs contrasted with elongated, thick hindlimbs supported by heavy shoulder and pelvic girdles.
The largest species, B. excelsus, reached lengths of 21 to 23 meters and weighed 15 to 20 tonnes.

The genus Brontosaurus was described by Othniel Charles Marsh in 1879, with the type species B. excelsus based on a partial skeleton without a skull found in Como Bluff, Wyoming, by William Harlow Reed.
Two other species, B. parvus and B. yahnahpin, were named in 1902 and 1994 respectively, though in 1902 Olof A. Peterson and Charles Gilmore named juvenile and adult skeletons Elosaurus parvus.
The animal is classified within the family Diplodocidae and belongs to the subfamily Apatosaurinae, which includes only Brontosaurus and Apatosaurus.
Brontosaurus fossils date to the Late Jurassic, specifically the Kimmeridgian to Tithonian stages, living between 156 and 146 million years ago in the Morrison Formation of Utah and Wyoming.
The species B. parvus specifically dates to the middle Kimmeridgian age.
Some paleontologists still debate whether Brontosaurus is a valid genus or a synonym of Apatosaurus, a view continued by John and ReBecca Foster.
In 1998 and supported in 2020, researchers suggested the Felch Quarry skull belongs to Brachiosaurus rather than Brontosaurus.
Robert T. Bakker argued in the 1990s that A. excelsus merits a separate genus distinct from A. ajax.

The original AMNH Brontosaurus mount featured a sculpted skull based on Camarasaurus bones, which was later found to be inaccurate compared to the delicate Diplodocus-like skull supported by McIntosh and Berman.
Marsh originally suggested Brontosaurus lacked intellect based on its small braincase and slender neural cord.
